title: 3rd Shift Weld & Assembly Team Lead - $750 Signing Bonus
description:
GENERAL SUMMARY
The Weld & Assembly Team Leader is responsible for providing day-to-day leadership and production support within assigned welding and assembly operations. This position works directly with production associates to ensure work is performed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with established quality, production, and standardized work requirements.
The Team Leader is a working leadership position responsible for coordinating manpower, monitoring production performance, supporting equipment and process issues, training and coaching associates, maintaining standardized work, and escalating conditions that may affect Safety, Quality, Delivery, Productivity, or Cost.
As a 3rd-shift floor leader, this position is expected to maintain a strong presence in the production area, respond to issues as they occur, make appropriate decisions within the authority of the position, and communicate unresolved concerns to the appropriate leadership and support departments.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide daily floor leadership and direction to associates within assigned welding and assembly operations.
Ensure associates follow established safety requirements, standardized work, quality standards, work instructions, and production procedures.
Coordinate daily manpower assignments based on production requirements, associate qualifications, attendance, and operational priorities.
Verify associates are properly trained and qualified before assigning them to equipment or processes.
Monitor production throughout the shift to ensure scheduled production requirements are achieved.
Review production performance, cycle times, downtime, scrap, quality concerns, and other operating conditions throughout the shift.
Respond promptly to production abnormalities and escalate equipment, quality, material, manpower, or process concerns when additional support is required.
Work closely with Weld Technicians, Maintenance, Quality, Material Handling, and other support functions to minimize production interruptions.
Support troubleshooting of robotic weld cells, automated assembly equipment, fixtures, tooling, and production processes within the scope of Team Leader training and responsibility.
Ensure equipment problems are communicated promptly and appropriate technical resources are contacted when required.
Verify proper start-up, changeover, and shutdown procedures are followed.
Support efficient job and model changeovers while maintaining required safety and quality standards.
Monitor parts and processes for compliance with established quality requirements.
Ensure required inspections, checks, testing, documentation, and production records are completed accurately and at the required frequency.
Immediately respond to suspected nonconforming product and ensure appropriate containment and escalation procedures are followed.
Ensure suspect or nonconforming material is properly identified, segregated, and controlled.
Work with Quality personnel to investigate and resolve product and process concerns.
Assist with containment, sorting, reinspection, and corrective actions when required.
Train, coach, and provide ongoing direction to production associates regarding standardized work, safety, quality, productivity, and job expectations.
Reinforce proper work methods and correct deviations from established standards.
Identify associates requiring additional training or coaching and communicate those needs to appropriate leadership.
Support cross-training and development of associates to improve flexibility and coverage within the department.
Monitor attendance and promptly communicate manpower or attendance concerns.
Ensure breaks, lunches, rotations, and relief are coordinated to support production requirements.
Maintain an active presence on the production floor and routinely verify conditions at assigned work areas.
Promote accountability while maintaining professional and respectful working relationships with associates.
Ensure production areas, equipment, workstations, aisles, and material locations are maintained in a clean, safe, and organized condition.
Support 5S, workplace organization, and continuous improvement activities.
Identify opportunities to reduce downtime, scrap, rework, unnecessary motion, material handling, and other forms of waste.
Participate in problem-solving and root-cause activities involving safety, quality, equipment, and production concerns.
Ensure required production, quality, downtime, scrap, and other shift documentation is completed accurately and timely.
Communicate significant events, open issues, temporary countermeasures, equipment conditions, quality concerns, and production status during shift handoff.
Escalate issues that cannot be resolved during the shift rather than allowing problems to continue without appropriate action.
Support overtime and alternate work schedules when required to meet production and customer needs.
Perform production work and provide relief or coverage when necessary while maintaining overall Team Leader responsibilities.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

SAFETY RESPONSIBILITIES
Safety is a primary responsibility of the Weld & Assembly Team Leader.
The Team Leader must:

Ensure associates follow all established safety policies, procedures, and work instructions.
Reinforce proper use of required personal protective equipment.
Ensure machine guarding, light curtains, interlocks, emergency stops, and other safety devices are properly used and never bypassed or defeated.
Immediately address unsafe acts and unsafe conditions.
Stop work or equipment when an immediate safety risk exists and escalate the condition appropriately.
Ensure associates follow applicable Lockout/Tagout requirements and never perform work for which they are not properly trained or authorized.
Maintain awareness of hazards associated with robotic weld cells, automated equipment, welding operations, material handling, and moving machinery.
Participate in safety investigations and corrective actions as required.
Encourage associates to identify and report hazards, near misses, and unsafe conditions.
Maintain good housekeeping and clear access to emergency equipment, exits, aisles, and work areas.

QUALITY RESPONSIBILITIES
The Team Leader is responsible for reinforcing quality at the source and ensuring established quality controls are followed throughout the shift.
Responsibilities include:

Ensure associates understand and follow applicable Control Plans, standardized work, work instructions, visual standards, inspection requirements, and quality alerts.
Verify required inspections and quality checks are completed at the specified frequency.
Ensure production associates understand applicable defect criteria and escalation requirements.
Respond immediately when a quality abnormality is identified.
Ensure suspect product is contained and controlled until proper disposition is determined.
Support Quality personnel during investigation, containment, and corrective-action activities.
Monitor recurring scrap, rework, weld, fit-up, dimensional, or assembly concerns and escalate trends appropriately.
Ensure process settings or equipment adjustments are not changed outside established authorization requirements.
Support prevention of nonconforming product from advancing to the next operation or customer.

PRODUCTION & LEADERSHIP RESPONSIBILITIES
The Team Leader is expected to understand the condition of the assigned production area throughout the shift, including:

Manpower and attendance.
Production schedule and priorities.
Production attainment versus plan.
Equipment status and downtime.
Quality concerns and containment activity.
Scrap and rework.
Material availability.
Associate training and qualification.
Safety concerns.
Open maintenance or technical issues.
Required follow-up for the incoming shift.

The Team Leader is expected to identify abnormalities early and take appropriate action rather than waiting until the end of the shift to report missed production or unresolved issues.

title: Director, Planning & Allocation Technology
description:
Vuori is one of the fastest-growing apparel brands in the world, and the way we plan and allocate product has to keep pace. We're looking for a technically strong product leader to own the strategy and roadmap for our merchandise planning and allocation capabilities — spanning pre-season and in-season planning, top-down and bottom-up, and how inventory flows to our stores and distribution centers. You'll partner with Data Science to put machine learning and advanced forecasting into the hands of our planners, work closely with Merchandising and Planning leadership to shape how that work actually gets done, and lead and grow a small team of Product Managers and Analysts. This is a role for someone as energized by explainability and user adoption as by the technology itself — because the best forecast in the world doesn't move the business if planners don't trust it.

What you'll get to do:

  • Own the product roadmap for our merchandise planning and allocation capabilities, prioritizing business impact, technical feasibility, and adoption of readiness.
  • Partner with Data Science as a technical peer to develop and productionize forecasting capabilities — machine learning models, probabilistic forecasting, and attribute-based new-item demand modeling — and own the explainability requirements that make planners trust them.
  • Drive adoption of system-generated forecasts as a primary measure of success and establish forecast accuracy and forecast value-add measurement, so model performance and business impact stay visible.
  • Partner with Planning, Merchandising, and Technology leadership to evolve the planning and allocation operating model around human-in-the-loop decision-making — helping define what the system decides, what the planner decides, and where exceptions escalate.
  • Keep a pulse on emerging technology across planning, forecasting, and AI, assessing what is genuinely production-ready and building it into the roadmap on a realistic timeline.
  • Own the product requirements for the data foundation behind planning intelligence, partnering with Data Engineering on pipeline timing, data quality, and the data products forecasting and allocation depend on.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a small team of Product Managers and Analysts, raising the bar on technical fluency, requirements of quality, and outcome of ownership.
  • Collaborate with on/offshore development partners on solution design and delivery and represent planning and allocation priorities in agile ceremonies and quarterly planning.

Who you are:

  • 10+ years in product management, analytics, or planning technology, with meaningful exposure to retail merchandise planning, allocation, or demand forecasting.
  • 2+ years managing or mentoring product managers or analysts, with the communication skills to explain technical trade-offs to merchants and planners, and business trade-offs to engineers and data scientists.
  • You have shipped a machine learning or advanced analytics capability into a business user's day-to-day workflow — not a dashboard, and not a proof of concept that stalled.
  • Technically fluent in forecasting: comfortable discussing model approaches, error metrics (WMAPE, bias, forecast value add), probabilistic versus point forecasts, and the trade-offs between accuracy and interpretability.
  • Strong working knowledge of merchandise planning and allocation — pre-season and in-season, top-down and bottom-up, open-to-buy, receipt flow, and store/DC allocation.
  • Experience working with on/offshore development teams in an Agile environment (JIRA, sprint and quarterly planning), plus hands-on familiarity with enterprise planning platforms (Anaplan, o9, RELEX, Blue Yonder, Board, or similar) from a data model and configuration perspective. Working knowledge of SQL is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of experience preferred.

Our investment in you:

At Vuori, we’re proud to offer the following to our employees:

  • Health Insurance
  • Savings and Retirement Plan
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Generous Vuori Discount & Industry Perks
  • Paid Time Off

title: Operations Associate (Hiring or Client Delivery)
description:
Grow our AI image service.

The role

We are Drop Zero Digital, a lifecycle marketing agency. We are hiring one person who is good at deciding. Our AI image service is our fastest-growing service, and whichever area you own, you will be helping it grow.

You will own one named area. Which one is decided during the trial rather than now, based on what you turn out to be strong at. It will be one of these two:

  1. The hiring machine. How we find, screen and hire people. Running the funnel end to end, sourcing, chasing, scheduling, keeping our tracker honest, and telling us when the process itself is broken.
  2. Client delivery operations. How work gets planned, briefed, chased and shipped for our clients. Holding timelines, briefing the team properly, and making sure nothing quietly stalls.

Both are the same job underneath: you notice what has slipped, you decide what to do, and you close it without being asked.

This is not an assistant job and it is not a coordinator job. You will make real calls every day, and you will be judged on the quality of those calls rather than on how much you got through.

We are building a team of people who decide well without being managed. If you want to be told what to do each morning, this job is not for you.

What we are looking for

  1. You make decisions and you own them, including the ones that go wrong.
  2. You can tell which calls are yours and which are not, and you get that split right in both directions.
  3. You take feedback as information and change, without folding on something you have good reason to believe.
  4. You get better fast. We would rather have someone at seventy percent climbing than someone flat at eighty five.
  5. You spot when something is failing and say so, including when it is our process and not your work.
  6. You write clearly and honestly, especially about problems.

On experience

We do not ask for a number of years and we do not screen on your CV, because we decide on what you do in the trial.

Whatever employment you do list, we verify: employer, dates, title and paid status, evidenced by contract and payslips, in one exchange. You need to have held a full-time job at some point in the last 12 months. Beyond that there is no minimum, and a short history costs you nothing here. Misrepresenting the history you do have is disqualifying. Tell us the true version and you will not be penalised for it.

How the process works, and we tell you all of it now

  1. Application and a short asynchronous interview. One take, no re-records.
  2. Aptitude tests, with a published floor.
  3. A short video introduction.
  4. A verification step where we check what you have told us.
  5. A short paid screen of a few days, then a paid trial of six to eight weeks doing the real job.

The trial is where the decision actually gets made, including which of the two areas you end up owning. From the first week you will be making calls on live work, and we will tell you straight how each one landed. It is paid from day one: half rate for the first two weeks while you find your feet, full rate from week three onward, and a completion payment when you finish the trial, whether or not we hire you. If we stop early, you are paid for the days you worked.

Requirements

  1. Full time once hired, and this is your only job. During the paid trial you work 4 hours a day with us, 2 of them at a fixed time inside our working day, and you can keep your current job. If you pass, you give notice and join us full time within 30 days.
  2. Reliable internet, at least 30 Mbps down and 5 Mbps up, tested live with us.
  3. Strong written English.
  4. Based in Indonesia.
  5. You track your working time with our time tracking tool from day one.

Benefits

1000 USD per month on hire, set by responsibility and demonstrated capability, not by how long you have worked.

Pass your 90-day review and your pay goes up by 50 percent. The 90 days count from the day you start full time.

On top of that:

  1. A one-month annual bonus (13th month pay in the Philippines and South Africa, THR in Indonesia).
  2. 15 days of paid leave a year, rising with tenure, plus your own country's public holidays.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (AI Products) | On-site | George WC
description:
Description

Senior Full-Stack Engineer (AI Products)

Location: George, Western Cape | On-site

AI agents aren’t products until people can use them. That’s where you come in.

About The Role

You’ll turn powerful AI systems into real, usable products; the kind customers and teams rely on every day. At ARC AI, we’re building intelligent agents that operate in a regulated insurance environment, and your role is to make them work in the real world.

This means designing and building the interfaces, APIs, and product layer that sit between AI and people. You’ll shape how users interact with AI: from chat interfaces and workflows to human-in-the-loop review systems that keep humans in control of agent decisions before they reach customers. Ensuring everything works smoothly, even when the AI doesn’t.

You’ll own the full stack: frontend experiences that handle streaming responses and unpredictable outputs, backend services that connect AI to core systems, and the pipelines that ship it all into production.

You’ll also build the observability and feedback loops that help us continuously improve how these agents perform in production, not just in evaluation, but in the real product.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role where what you build is the product, seen and used by customers and leadership alike.

Requirements

About you

  • You’re an experienced full-stack engineer who has already shipped AI-powered products into production.
  • You understand that building for AI is different. You’ve worked with non-deterministic systems, handled variable latency, and designed experiences that gracefully manage failure, partial responses, and uncertainty.

You’re Confident Across The Stack

  • Modern frontend frameworks (React or similar)
  • Backend/API development (Node.js, Python, or similar)
  • REST/GraphQL APIs at scale
  • Secure, compliant data handling in regulated environments
  • You’ve built systems where reliability, security, and control matter, including authentication, validation, and enforcing boundaries at the API layer (not relying on the model to behave).
  • You’re also comfortable owning the full lifecycle: from design and development to CI/CD and deployment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience demonstrating shipped production AI work.
  • 5+ years’ experience in full-stack software engineering roles.
  • Demonstrated experience shipping user-facing AI or LLM-powered products into production environments.

Bonus points

We’d love to hear from you if you’ve also worked with:

  • Conversational interfaces, Azure, or LLM observability tools
  • Complex system integrations like CRM platforms
  • Training or certifications in secure software development or data protection (e.g. GDPR/POPIA awareness)

Most importantly, you think like a product engineer. You care about how things work in production, not just how they’re built.

Why join us

You’ll be part of a small, high-impact team building something from the ground up. There are no layers of separation, no handoffs to QA, DevOps, or external teams. You own what you build.

Your work will directly shape how AI is experienced by real customers in a regulated environment. It’s complex, meaningful, and visible.

We’re based in George, Western Cape, and this role is office-based, giving you the opportunity to collaborate closely, move quickly, and build as a team.

If you’ve built AI products that made it into users’ hands and you’re ready to take full ownership of what comes next, we’d like to hear from you.

title: Principal HRIS Analyst
description:
Principal HRIS Analyst - hybrid role based in Lexington, MA


About Mimecast


The work people build is worth protecting, and it's harder to protect than it used to be. AI agents now move at machine speed with human-level access, and a small slip-up can become a very public one. We disrupt cybercriminal activity before that happens. We think fast, go big, and always demand more of ourselves. We work hard, deliver, and repeat. We grow with real determination and put success well within reach. We push each other to be better and expect to be pushed back, in a community built on respect, where everyone is counted. Work Protected.


Overview


HRIS & Analytics is looking for a Principal Workday Analyst to own the Workday configuration behind Mimecast’s global compensation and benefits programs, translating Total Rewards and HR requirements into scalable system design across 14 countries and currencies. The role sits within the HRIS & Analytics team, which is optimizing a mature, fully deployed Workday environment. You’ll own Compensation and Benefits configuration end to end, contribute to Core HCM alongside the broader team, and report to the Director, HR Tech & Analytics. This position is in our Lexington, MA offices and has a hybrid work schedule (minimum 2 days per week).


What You'll Do

  • Serve as the subject matter expert for Workday Compensation and Benefits, partnering with Total Rewards, HR Business Partners, and regional HR leads to translate business needs into scalable configuration.
  • Lead the configuration, testing, and deployment of new compensation and benefits functionality, including annual merit, bonus, and open enrollment cycles.
  • Contribute to Core HCM configuration and business process design as part of the wider HRIS team’s shared workload.
  • Own end-to-end testing for compensation and benefits changes, including regression testing tied to Workday’s biannual releases.
  • Maintain data integrity and security for compensation and benefits domains, including auditing security groups and access to sensitive pay data.
  • Build and maintain reports and dashboards that support compensation planning, benefits administration, and HR decision-making.
  • Document configuration decisions, business process changes, and standard operating procedures so knowledge is shared across the team.
  • Mentor other members of the HRIS team on compensation and benefits configuration and act as an escalation point for complex issues.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify and standardize configuration as the environment matures rather than layering on new complexity.

What You'll Bring

  • Deep Workday experience, including advanced hands-on configuration expertise in Advanced Compensation and Benefits and the autonomy to own complex, end-to-end solutions in a global, multi-country environment.
  • Working knowledge of at least one additional Workday module beyond Compensation and Benefits, such as Core HCM, Absence, Performance, Recruiting, Security, or Advanced Reporting.
  • Experience supporting compensation and benefits programs across multiple countries, with an understanding of how local requirements shape system design.
  • The ability to manage a Workday release cycle end to end, from reviewing release notes and assessing impact through testing and rollout.
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, balanced with the ability to explain technical configuration clearly to non-technical stakeholders.
  • The judgment and discretion required to handle highly sensitive compensation and personal data.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Workday Pro certification in Compensation, Benefits, or Advanced Compensation.
  • Experience with EIB loads, Workday Studio, or Core Connectors for benefits or payroll integrations.
  • Exposure to Workday Extend or advanced custom reporting, including calculated fields and matrix reports.
  • Experience mentoring junior analysts or leading small configuration projects.

The base salary range for this position is $132,000 - 198,000 USD plus benefits. This range represents the minimum and maximum new hire compensation for this role. The position may also be eligible for incentive plans and additional benefits, in accordance with company policy and local regulations. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location with individual compensation also dependent on factors such as qualifications, experience, and skills. Final offers will reflect these considerations and may vary accordingly.

Coveo is looking for a Software Development intern to join our DevTooling team within Platform Engineering, where you’ll contribute to the tools and infrastructure used by developers across R&D. Your mission? Help improve our software delivery lifecycle, contribute to our CI/CD ecosystem, and gain hands‑on experience with DevOps and infrastructure technologies at scale. As part of the DevTooling team, you’ll contribute to the tools and infrastructure that developers across Coveo rely on every day. You’ll gain hands‑on experience with Python, Kubernetes, GitOps, and modern CI/CD practices, while learning how software is built, deployed, and maintained at scale.

Your impact, day to day:

  • Engage actively in daily stand‑up meetings to discuss progress, roadblocks, and plans. Collaborate with team members to ensure alignment and effective communication.
  • Manage and resolve assigned Jira tickets, ensuring timely completion of tasks.
  • Contribute to real‑world projects that will be implemented for Coveo’s clients. This can include coding, testing, and deploying solutions that meet customer requirements and enhance their experience.
  • Develop your skills by drawing on the expertise of experienced developers around you. Ask questions, explore new technologies, and apply best practices related to software development, infrastructure, and delivery.
  • Take an active role in code review sessions. Offer constructive feedback and receive advice on how to raise the quality of your code, follow best practices and strengthen your programming skills.

The Essentials:

  • You are currently studying Software Engineering or Computer Science in a Bachelor's degree or higher in the province of Québec.
  • You are able to work from one of our offices 2 days a week. Our hybrid work model offers flexibility, you can benefit from face‑to‑face learning from your team on office days while home days allow you to focus and complete complex work.
  • You are legally entitled to work full‑time in Canada for the duration of the 15 week internship.

Think you’ve got what it takes?

  • You have experience with Python.
  • You have completed an internship.
  • You have a strong sense of ownership and are proud of what you create.
  • You’re a collaborative team player who asks questions, shares ideas, and enjoys solving problems with others.
  • You’re curious about DevOps, infrastructure, and CI/CD, and interested in learning technologies such as Kubernetes, ArgoCD, GitOps, and Terraform.
  • You’ve participated in some hackathons and/or have a few personal projects.

Join the Coveolife!

We encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of, for example, age, gender, disability, gaps in CV, national or ethnic background.

title: Design Director
description:
Out client is a US-headquartered, full-lifecycle product development company with 250+ team members across the US, Europe (Poland, Romania, Ukraine), and LATAM (Colombia, Brazil). They partner with Fortune 500 companies and well-funded startups to deliver world-class software products — from ideation and design through engineering and launch. Interesting Facts:

- Over 270 team members.

  • Fully remote - we let people work where they work best.
    - They work with clients who value our opinion and thought leadership and where we can make a meaningful contribution to architectural decisions, engineering decisions, and product decisions.

    - 100% remote work

title: Facilities Maintenance Lead Technician
description:
IPG Photonics is revolutionizing the laser industry as the pioneering developer and leading producer of fiber lasers and amplifiers. Headquartered in Marlborough, MA, IPG has over 4,800 employees in more than 30 locations around the world. We aspire to work together with our employees and customers to apply light in ways that improve life.

Our mission is to develop innovative laser solutions to make the world a better place. To accomplish this mission, we are committed to attracting and retaining the best talent and an engaged, diverse, and thriving workforce that drives a sustainable future for our company and society.

Working at IPG Photonics you can expect challenging projects, a motivating and friendly environment, and competitive benefits.

The Facilities Technician (Lead) is the most experienced hands-on facilities role, acting as the primary point of technical escalation and informal team leader for the facilities group. This role advises on preventive maintenance strategy, leads reliability and improvement initiatives, provides backup coverage for building automation and controls as needed, manages vendor and contractor relationships for larger or specialized projects, and mentors less experienced technicians and maintenance workers — without formal people-management accountability.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership & Facility Strategy

  • Serve as the primary point of escalation for complex, non-routine, or previously unencountered facility issues.
  • Determine methods and procedures for new or ambiguous assignments where no established process exists.
  • Own and continuously improve the preventive maintenance program, including PM schedules, asset criticality, and CMMS or IWMS data quality.
  • Lead root-cause analysis on recurring failures and drive corrective and preventive actions to reduce downtime and repeat repairs.
  • Provide input on capital planning, budget awareness, and long-range maintenance and reliability initiatives.
  • Provide backup coverage for the site building automation system (BAS) as needed — recognizing and responding to alarms, making routine schedule and setpoint adjustments, and escalating to the controls contractor as needed. Site-specific platform training is provided on the job.

Coaching, Coordination & Vendor Management

  • Act as informal team leader for the facilities and maintenance group, coordinating daily work assignments and priorities.
  • Coach, mentor, and up-skill Facilities Technicians; support onboarding and training plans.
  • Own vendor and contractor relationships for larger, specialized, or capital-project work — scoping work, reviewing quotes, and overseeing quality of completed work.
  • Lead facility renovations, equipment moves, and workspace reconfiguration projects from planning through completion.

Safety & Compliance

  • Lead routine and ad hoc safety and compliance inspections; own remediation tracking to closure.
  • Ensure facility work and contractor work meet OSHA requirements, company policy, and applicable building codes.
  • Serve as a key contact during emergency response, storm preparation, and facility shutdown and startup, coordinating cross-shift and cross-team response.
  • Maintain and audit maintenance records, inspection logs, and compliance documentation for accuracy and completeness.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
Who we are

Arkeus builds AI-powered sensing systems that help autonomous platforms detect, track and understand what's happening in the most complex and contested environments. Our technology is deployed across defence and national security applications — already protecting lives and strengthening security across the U.S. and allied markets.

Backed by QIC, Main Sequence, R+VC, Salus Ventures, Folklore Ventures, DYNE Ventures and Beaten Zone Venture Partners, Arkeus is entering a major growth phase. We are a small, fast-moving company with the energy and ambition of a start-up and the technical credibility of a world-class defence technology provider.

We work at the intersection of optics, autonomy, robotics and real-time AI and we deploy what we build. If you want to ship technology that matters, not technology that ships decks, this is where you belong.

Check it yourself on News | Arkeus

We have developed an inclusive, transparent and engaging culture that focuses on building a diverse workforce — realising that to attract the very best, we need to ensure our culture is ready to welcome people from all ages, genders and backgrounds.

About the role

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Arkeus, you will work with the Machine Learning team to prepare data and develop ML models, joining specialists working at the intersection of machine learning, computer vision, optical science and engineering design.

Your work will be central to our image-based optical sensing technology — training, optimising and deploying models that detect and classify objects from the airborne perspective, in real time, on real hardware.

You will take ownership of models and components across the full ML lifecycle — from data pipelines through to models running on edge devices — working alongside senior ML and computer vision engineers, translating state-of-the-art research into deployed capability, and helping guide and review the work of more junior engineers as the team grows.


About you

  • An engineer with hands-on machine learning experience, ready to take on ownership and complex problems.
  • A graduate in a relevant discipline, with demonstrated professional or research experience building and deploying ML models.
  • Able to take a machine learning problem from idea to deployed result — independently, and demonstrated through professional work, research, or substantial personal projects.
  • Enjoys reading research, experimenting and asking good questions.
  • Wants to see your models running in the real world, not sitting in a notebook.

Key responsibilities

  • Implement and improve the ETL process.
  • Make data readily available to engineers across the team and improve and organise our datasets.
  • Use PyTorch, OpenCV and scikit-learn to design, build and train neural networks for image classification and object detection.
  • Lead the implementation and optimisation of state-of-the-art deep-learned neural networks in computer vision applications.
  • Contribute to and take ownership of accurate object detection across varied environments (over sea, littoral zone, rural and city) and at various target sizes.
  • Participate in team meetings, conduct code reviews, and help uphold engineering standards across the team.
  • Support and mentor junior engineers, sharing knowledge and good practice.
  • Report software bugs and issues in the issue-tracking system in a timely manner.
  • Develop and maintain documentation.

Your experience and skills

  • Tertiary qualification (Bachelor's or Master's) in computer science, engineering, mathematics or a related discipline.
  • 2-4 years of demonstrated machine learning experience through professional work, research, or substantial personal projects.
  • Confident working in Python, with solid hands-on experience in PyTorch.
  • Strong understanding of the fundamentals of neural networks and convolutional neural networks (CNNs).
  • Hands-on experience with object detection and/or segmentation problems.
  • Familiarity with common libraries such as scikit-learn, scikit-image, PIL, Pandas and OpenCV.
  • Sound research practices — able to read, understand and apply findings from technical literature.
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain an Australian Defence security clearance.

Desirable:

  • Exposure to C++.
  • Experience with data science workflows and data pipelines.
  • Technical experience reading from and controlling cameras.
  • Experience deploying and optimising models on edge devices or embedded hardware.
  • Exposure to airborne remote sensing, GIS or optical technologies.
  • Strong physics and mathematics background.
  • Examples of personal or open-source technical projects (GitHub links welcome).

Why Join Arkeus

  • You will work on the hardest problems in deep-tech — optics, autonomy, real-time AI and hardware-software integration in a single product. The gap between what you build and where it ends up is almost nonexistent.
  • You will collaborate with exceptional leaders who have 40+ years of combined experience in autonomy, optics and defence. You will be learning from — and contributing to — the best in the field.
  • You will become part of a close-knit, ego-free team where ideas compete on merit, not seniority. Low politics, high trust. The kind of team you will still be talking about in ten years.
  • You will work hard and be expected to bring your best — and in return, you will grow faster than you ever would at a large organisation.
  • You will work on technology that is already deployed in real environments — protecting lives and strengthening security across defence and national security applications.
  • You will receive a competitive, market-benchmarked salary, structured career pathways built to grow with you, and the opportunity to participate in our Employee Share Option Plan (ESOP).

If this sounds like you, please apply even if you don't check every box — we care more about how you think than whether your CV is perfect. Join our growing team and help us change the world through autonomous systems.

title: Systems Engineer
description:
The Elevator Pitch

Are you ready to be the backbone of the systems and infrastructure that keep a fast-growing security technology company running smoothly? Do you enjoy owning the day-to-day platforms, systems, and cloud infrastructure that the whole business depends on?

Evolv is seeking a Systems Engineer to administer, operate, and continuously improve our core IT systems—from Microsoft 365 and virtualization to cloud infrastructure and disaster recovery. Reporting to the Senior Director of Cybersecurity & Technology, you'll be the reliable technical engine behind Evolv's IT operations, working alongside a Network & Cybersecurity Engineer peer who owns network and security.

You'll collaborate across the organization, build trusted partnerships with stakeholders, and serve as a subject matter expert on day-to-day systems and cloud operations. If you're energized by keeping complex systems running smoothly and making every employee's day a little easier, this role is for you.

Success in the Role: What are performance outcomes over the first 6-12 months you will work toward completing?

In the first 30 days, you will:

  • Get to know the IT team and the systems/platforms they currently support
  • Start building relationships with key stakeholders throughout the company
  • Gain familiarity with the current systems toolstack: Microsoft 365, virtualization/backup infrastructure, AWS/Azure, and disaster recovery processes
  • Learn Evolv's data management practices and how systems operations supports them

Within 3 months, you will:

  • Begin implementing or improving processes that measurably reduce operational risk and downtime
  • Build trust-based relationships with peers in IT and key stakeholders across business units
  • Become an established subject matter expert on Evolv's systems, virtualization, and cloud infrastructure
  • Take ownership of offsite/disaster recovery replication and testing cadence

By the end of the first year, you will:

  • Be recognized as a trusted subject matter expert across systems administration, virtualization, and cloud operations
  • Have driven measurable improvements to IT operational maturity and resilience
  • Successfully supported corporate data management initiatives, including classification, retention, and deletion practices
  • Developed and documented systems and processes that empower the broader IT team and reduce single points of failure
  • Be seen as a go-to resource by colleagues across the company for day-to-day systems questions and best practice guidance

The Work: What type of work will you be doing? What assignments, requirements, or skills will you be performing on a regular basis?

Systems, Infrastructure & Operations:

  • Administer Microsoft 365, including Exchange, Teams, and SharePoint
  • Own virtualization (Nutanix) and backup (Rubrik) infrastructure, including Windows and Linux guest VMs
  • Manage offsite/disaster recovery replication and testing
  • Support corporate data management initiatives: data classification, retention, and deletion
  • Operate day-to-day AWS/Azure infrastructure: EC2, S3, resource groups, cost management and budgeting
  • Provide front-line escalation support and mentoring to IT teammates; maintain runbooks and documentation
  • Act as a trusted technology advisor to internal stakeholders on day-to-day systems needs

Leadership, Team Structure & Culture

You will join the IT organization as a direct report to the Senior Director of Cybersecurity & Technology, working alongside a Network & Cybersecurity Engineer peer who owns network infrastructure and security operations.

This is a hands-on, collaborative team that takes security and operational excellence seriously. This is a senior individual contributor role focused on deep technical impact—your job is to keep Evolv's enterprise systems, services, and cloud infrastructure running smoothly through the processes and automation you build. You'll have meaningful autonomy over how you approach problems and are actively encouraged to bring creative solutions, identify improvement opportunities, and advocate for better ways of working.

You'll work alongside teammates who share your drive for continuous improvement, and you'll have a manager who values initiative, trusts the team to execute, and wants to hear your ideas.

Where is the role located?

This role is based out of Evolv HQ in Waltham, Massachusetts. This is a hybrid role with an expectation of 3 days per week on-site. Fully remote candidates will not be considered.

Compensation and Transparency Statement

The base salary range for this full-time position is $102,000-$166,000. In addition to base salary, this role offers a competitive target bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. This range reflects our commitment to pay transparency and equity, in alignment with applicable state laws. Our compensation ranges are determined based on factors such as role, level, location, market benchmarks, and internal equity. The posted range represents the good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this role across U.S. locations. Actual compensation within the range will be based on the candidate’s skills, experience, education, and geographic location.

In accordance with state and local pay transparency laws—including those in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, and others—we disclose salary ranges in all job postings and provide additional information upon request.

During the hiring process, your recruiter will share:

• The specific salary range for your preferred location

• A general overview of our benefits and equity offerings

• Insights into how compensation decisions are made, including factors that influence starting pay

We are committed to fair pay practices, and we regularly review our compensation programs to ensure they are competitive, equitable, and aligned with our values.

Benefits

At Evolv, we’re on a mission to help make public spaces safer through innovative security technology. So, we're looking for future teammates who embody our values, people who:

  • Do the right thing, always;
  • Put people first'
  • Own it;
  • Win together; and continue to
  • Be bold, stay curious.

Our Benefits Include:

  • Equity as part of your total compensation package
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Health Savings Account (HSA)
  • A 401(k) plan (and 2% company match)
  • Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO)- take the time you need to recharge, with manager approval and business needs in mind
  • Quarterly stipend for perks and benefits that matter most to you
  • Tuition reimbursement to support your ongoing learning and development
  • Subscription to Calm

title: Senior Spacecraft Propulsion Test Engineer II
description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SPACE SYSTEMS

At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more.

Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions.

SENIOR SPACECRAFT PROPULSION TEST ENGINEER II

As a Senior Spacecraft Propulsion Test Engineer II on our propulsion engineering team based out of Long Beach, CA, your purpose will be to plan, prepare for, and execute engine and propulsion component testing. This includes ownership of the test facility, equipment, and test operations. You will play a critical role in successful development, qualification, and production testing, which directly results in the success of our missions and products. As part of the propulsion development team, you will be involved with engine and propulsion system development from cradle-to-grave, providing test-driven insights that improve the reliability, manufacturability, testability, and performance of our products.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

  • Set and maintain best practices for all aspects of testing, ensuring a high standard of excellence across the team
  • Provide guidance, training, mentorship, and technical leadership to team members on testing methodologies and processes
  • Review and sign off on test plans and test reports, ensuring quality and compliance with requirements
  • Support engineers and leadership with risk-based decision making to guide the team through development challenges
  • Own the full testing lifecycle, including test planning, setup, instrumentation, execution, data analysis, and reporting
  • Apply a systems engineering mindset to testing activities, integrating with broader engineering efforts
  • Communicate regularly and effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, both internal and external to the team
  • Define, document, and uphold standards of excellence through training, coaching, and review of others’ work
  • Contribute to meaningful, career-defining projects alongside exceptional colleagues in a collaborative environment

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 8+ years of experience in rocket engine test engineering, or equivalent high-performance field
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, (aerospace, mechanical, mechatronics, or other technical engineering discipline)
  • Ability to travel to test facilities and work off-site for extended periods
  • Prior work on engine test facilities and experience hot fire testing liquid rocket engines, including instrumentation, test operation, and data analysis
  • Expertise in instrumentation, automation, and data acquisition using either National Instruments or Beckhoff PLC

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience working with hypergolic propellants, or experience designing, building, or maintaining flight or GSE systems for hypergolic propellant service
  • Excited by the opportunity to establish a new capability for Rocket Lab and the country
  • Great communication skills and the ability to lead a team to execute a technical project. This requires an understanding of the fundamentals of technical project management and systems engineering to manage interfaces and deliverables across all teams involved
  • Genuine passion for engineering, strong attention to detail, and an eagerness to learn
  • Excellent documentation and organization of engineering information, including test plans, test reports, facility configuration management, etc.
  • Track record of successfully investigating and resolving the root causes of anomalies during testing or flight
  • Strong understanding of standard aerospace testing including random vibration, shock, thermal cycle, thermal vacuum, helium leak, accelerated life, and margined performance testing
  • Experience with getting government approvals through NEPA, permitting, or similar processes for construction, industrial, or test operations
  • Capabilities using Python for data manipulation and post-processing
  • Experience with 1D fluid system modelling
  • Master's or PhD

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

Anticipated annual equity grant value is designed around function, level, experience, and other factors; realized value depends on vesting and stock-price performance.

Join one of the world's fastest-growing space companies and own a piece of it. In addition to competitive base pay, you'll receive company stock as part of your total compensation package, giving you a direct stake in our success. As we expand to new launch sites, groundbreaking missions, and global markets, your ownership has the opportunity to grow alongside the company.

Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.

Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.

Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Total Compensation (base and equity)
$165,000—$277,000 USD
Base Salary
$132,000—$220,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

title: VP, Global Medical Affairs
description:
Primary Function:

The VP, Global Medical Affairs will build and lead Zai Lab's Global Medical Affairs organization, with primary emphasis on the US and other regions outside China. This leader will establish the vision, strategy, organizational capabilities, and operating infrastructure required to support the company's first global launch and expanding pipeline. The role will serve as the senior Medical Affairs leader for global programs across the oncology and immunology portfolio, driving scientific leadership, evidence generation, external engagement, and cross-functional collaboration to maximize the value of Zai Lab's medicines throughout their lifecycle.

This position is based in our South San Francisco, CA office.

Major Responsibilities and Duties:

Medical Affairs Strategy & Organizational Leadership

  • Define and own the Medical Affairs strategy for Zai Lab's global oncology and immunology portfolio, providing leadership for global medical priorities, scientific engagement, and evidence generation. Foster strong partnership with Medical Affairs leadership in China to ensure a coordinated and aligned approach to global programs.
  • Provide executive-level scientific leadership and represent Medical Affairs across internal governance bodies, executive leadership forums, and cross-functional decision-making processes.
  • Ensure all medical affairs activities comply with applicable regulations, industry standards (PhRMA, OIG), and internal policies; lead development and continuous improvement of Medical Affairs SOPs and governance frameworks; oversee Medical Information operations and respond to escalated medical inquiries.

Pre-Launch & Launch Readiness

  • Develop and execute comprehensive pre-launch Medical Affairs plans for global pipeline assets in the US and other regions outside China, establishing the scientific and clinical foundation ahead of commercial launch.
  • Partner with Regulatory Affairs on US label development, lifecycle management, and Health Authority interactions, including FDA advisory committees and scientific advice meetings.
  • Lead KOL identification, mapping, and engagement strategies across key oncology centers and academic institutions; establish peer-level relationships with thought leaders in SCLC, neuroendocrine carcinomas, and other priority indications.
  • Partner with Commercial and Market Access teams to ensure scientific communication readiness, payer evidence packages, and HEOR alignment as commercial infrastructure is built out.

Evidence Generation & Scientific Communication

  • Develop and oversee evidence generation plans across the US and other regions outside China, including IIS programs, real-world evidence (RWE) initiatives, and collaborative research studies in partnership with academic and community oncology centers.
  • Lead the publication strategy and oversight for global Medical Affairs programs, ensuring high-quality, timely dissemination of clinical data at key oncology congresses (ASCO, AACR, ASH, ESMO) and in peer-reviewed journals.
  • Oversee the development of scientific communication materials, medical education content, and advisory board programs that accurately reflect the clinical data and support appropriate use.
  • Champion competitive intelligence and landscape analysis, translating insights into actionable medical strategy.

External Stakeholder & Patient Advocacy Engagement

  • Engage key oncology cooperative groups, professional societies, and academic networks to advance disease education and support Zai Lab’s scientific reputation.
  • Own the patient advocacy strategy for the US and other regions outside China; build relationships with relevant patient advocacy organizations, integrate patient perspectives into medical strategy, and support disease awareness and education initiatives.
  • Represent Zai Lab at national and international medical congresses, scientific symposia, and regulatory interactions as appropriate.
  • Work effectively across global time zones and travel up to 25%.

People Leadership & Operations

  • Build and lead a high-performing Medical Affairs team supporting the US and other regions outside China, while partnering closely with Medical Affairs leadership in China on global programs and cross-regional coordination; recruit, develop, and retain top scientific talent, establishing clear accountability, performance metrics, and development plans while fostering a culture of scientific rigor, patient-centricity, and integrity.
  • Oversee departmental budget planning, resource allocation, and agency/vendor governance to ensure operational excellence.

REQUIRED:

  • MD with 12 years of progressive experience in medical affairs within the biopharmaceutical industry.

PREFERRED:

  • Clinical background in oncology or hematology; experience in precision oncology, ADCs, or immuno-oncology; existing KOL network in SCLC, lung cancers, or neuroendocrine carcinomas.
  • Demonstrated track record of building and leading global or US medical affairs organizations, including pre-launch, launch, and in-line medical support for oncology or specialty assets; proven ability to partner cross-functionally with Commercial, Market Access, Regulatory, and Clinical Development.
  • Deep expertise in US and global medical affairs operations: MSL programs, evidence generation, publication planning, medical education, advisory boards, and medical information.
  • Proven pre-launch and launch medical affairs leadership, including HEOR and market access medical strategy integration; experience in a global US/China operating environment or cross-border clinical and regulatory programs is a plus.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with demonstrated success building medical affairs organizations in high-growth, pre-commercial or early commercial US biotech settings.
  • Strong scientific acumen with the ability to translate complex clinical data into compelling medical narratives; excellent communication and executive presence, comfortable engaging KOLs, health authorities, and C-suite stakeholders.
  • Ability to work across several time zones and travel internationally.
  • Experience in cross-regional collaboration including Asia/China.
  • Maintains the highest standards of integrity and ethics.

The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be between $369K and $536K/year; however, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a sign-on bonus, restricted stock units, and discretionary awards in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. title: Lead Data Scientist
description:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the Team

Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres and regulators to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges, and help to democratise health for all.

About the role

As a Lead Data Scientist, you'll take on a pivotal, entrepreneurial role, functioning as the technical expert who thrives on complexity and commercial impact. You will be responsible for setting the technical direction and ensuring the high-quality, scalable delivery of our most challenging, high-impact projects.

This position combines deep expertise in machine learning with strategic oversight to define project roadmaps, manage technical risk, and architect reliable solutions. Your focus will be on driving innovation, mentoring cross-functional teams, and actively shaping both our technical standards and long-term customer relationships.

What you'll be doing:

  • Setting the technical direction for complex, business-critical projects and expertly balancing trade-offs between speed, innovation, and reliability.

  • Designing and implementing reliable, production-grade technical solutions, ensuring comprehensive documentation of architectures and specifications.

  • Defining project problems, developing clear roadmaps, and overseeing end-to-end delivery across multi-disciplinary workstreams.

  • Leading technical scoping and feasibility studies for high-value sales opportunities and strategic customer engagements.

  • Managing relationships and communications with technical stakeholders, fostering trust and aligning technical solutions with shared long-term commercial goals.

  • Driving the adoption of best practices, shared resources, and robust technical processes across the wider Data Science craft.

  • Mentoring and developing other data scientists and team members, actively contributing to the growth and technical excellence of the organisation.

Who we're looking for:

  • You have proven project management expertise, capable of dividing complex, ill-defined problems into actionable, clearly defined workstreams with timelines you can defend.

  • You possess strong customer leadership skills, able to act as a trusted technical advisor and drive long-term strategic relationships with demanding clients.

  • You bring depth of expertise in at least one machine learning domain and strong technical breadth across the entire data science landscape.

  • You are a skilled technical leader, proficient in mentoring individuals, managing teams (including other managers), and rolling out impactful tools and workflows.

  • You are adept at managing ill-defined, high-risk tasks, consistently delivering innovative and practical outcomes under commercial pressure.

  • You excel at cross-functional collaboration, effectively aligning technical strategy with Engineering, Commercial, and Infrastructure teams.

  • You have experience extending technical oversight to business unit-level initiatives, using your vision to influence and contribute to organisational success.

The Interview Process

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

  2. Introduction to the team (30 minutes)

  3. Take Home Technical Assessment

  4. Technical Interview (90 minutes)

  5. Commercial Interview (60 minutes)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: MAC Organizer I
description:
SEIU Local 2015 – Member Action Center Organizer I

Location: California – Member Action Center
Department: Member Action Center
Reports To: MAC Director or Designee
Status: Full-Time

About SEIU Local 2015

SEIU Local 2015 is the largest union of long-term care workers in California, representing more than half a million home care, skilled nursing facility, and assisted living center workers across the state. Our members are united in their commitment to caring for California’s older adults and people with disabilities while building worker power and stronger communities.

Our mission is to unleash the collective power of long-term care workers, their families, and their communities to advance economic and social justice. We are committed to building an anti-racist organization grounded in equity, justice, and cross-difference solidarity.

To learn more, visit seiu2015.org.

About the Role

SEIU Local 2015 is seeking a compassionate, solutions-oriented, and member-focused Member Action Center Organizer I to support long-term care workers through the union’s Member Action Center (MAC).

The Member Action Center is a high-volume, inbound service and organizing center that serves as a primary point of contact for union members. The MAC Organizer I helps workers understand and exercise their workplace and union rights, access available benefits and training opportunities, address work-related concerns, and become more actively involved in their union.

Through telephone, electronic, and written communication, the MAC Organizer I listens carefully to members, identifies their needs, provides accurate information, documents each interaction, resolves matters within the position’s scope, and routes complex issues to the appropriate staff team for follow-up. The position works closely with union officers, managers, field staff, internal departments, members, and the California Long-Term Care Education Center.

This is more than a traditional customer-service role. The MAC Organizer I uses every member interaction as an opportunity to build trust, strengthen union participation, develop worker leadership, and connect members to collective action. The ideal candidate is calm under pressure, highly organized, comfortable working with technology, and committed to providing respectful and accurate service in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

Member Service & Call-Center Operations

  • Answer a high volume of inbound calls and place outbound follow-up calls using a computer-based telephone system
  • Communicate with members through telephone, email, mail, text, and other approved channels
  • Use active listening and effective questioning to understand each member’s needs, concerns, and requested support
  • Follow approved call flows, scripts, standard operating procedures, and escalation protocols while providing individualized and respectful service
  • Provide clear, accurate, and accessible information within the scope of the position
  • Place callers on hold, transfer or conference calls, initiate help-desk support, and connect members with appropriate internal or external resources when necessary
  • De-escalate concerns, respond professionally to complaints, and help members understand available options and next steps
  • Complete required follow-up actions, mail requests, referrals, work orders, and escalations accurately and within established timelines
  • Maintain professional phone etiquette and create a high-quality service experience during every member interaction

Member Organizing & Union Engagement

  • Help form, build, and grow the union through meaningful interactions with members and represented workers
  • Educate members about the union’s mission, programs, campaigns, services, priorities, and opportunities for participation
  • Engage members regarding issues affecting long-term care workers, including workplace rights, public policy, political developments, contract campaigns, benefits, training, and member programs
  • Encourage member participation in union meetings, trainings, actions, campaigns, leadership opportunities, and other organizational activities
  • Support membership recruitment and retention by answering questions regarding membership status, dues, union participation, and the value of collective action
  • Conduct membership and Committee on Political Education (COPE) sign-up conversations as assigned
  • Encourage civic engagement, including voter registration, get-out-the-vote activities, grassroots advocacy, legislative action, and other approved political programs
  • Identify members who may be interested in deeper union involvement or leadership and refer them to the appropriate organizing or departmental staff
  • Communicate member concerns, emerging themes, and organizing opportunities to MAC leadership and relevant departments

Workplace, Contract & Grievance Support

  • Respond to general questions regarding collective bargaining agreements, workplace rights, employer practices, and available union processes
  • Conduct first-level intake and information gathering for workplace complaints, discipline concerns, grievances, requests, and other member issues
  • Review the information provided, ask appropriate follow-up questions, and document the relevant facts accurately and objectively
  • Provide members with approved information regarding processes, expectations, timelines, and next steps without exceeding the scope of the position
  • Create and route grievance requests, case referrals, work orders, or escalations to the staff teams responsible for collective bargaining, employer relations, representation, or field follow-up
  • Identify urgent, sensitive, or high-risk concerns and escalate them promptly in accordance with established procedures
  • Track assigned follow-up activities and help ensure members receive appropriate communication regarding their concerns
  • Maintain neutrality, discretion, and confidentiality when handling sensitive member, employment, disciplinary, or organizational information

Benefits, Training & Resource Navigation

  • Answer general questions about employment-related benefits and direct members to appropriate resources for additional assistance
  • Assist workers with training-course registration and questions regarding programs offered through the California Long-Term Care Education Center
  • Follow established procedures to verify eligibility for health insurance benefits and other member programs
  • Provide accurate information regarding available education, training, benefit, and support resources
  • Assist members in completing required steps, locating forms, understanding instructions, and connecting with the appropriate program administrator
  • Use approved translation and interpretation resources, including LanguageLine, to support members who communicate in languages other than English
  • Document assistance provided, outstanding needs, and required follow-up in the appropriate system

Case Documentation & Data Integrity

  • Document every member interaction accurately, objectively, and promptly in designated MAC databases and systems
  • Review and update member information, call notes, case details, follow-up records, and other required data
  • Create online work orders, escalations, referrals, mail requests, and case records using approved forms and workflows
  • Select accurate issue categories, dispositions, outcomes, and referral pathways
  • Maintain complete records that enable other staff and departments to understand the matter and continue service without requiring the member to repeat their experience unnecessarily
  • Protect confidential member, employment, benefits, financial, political, and organizational information
  • Correct identified documentation errors promptly and participate in quality-review or coaching processes
  • Complete required activity, service, organizing, and performance reports within established deadlines

Quality, Productivity & Departmental Accountability

  • Meet established expectations for call handling, service quality, schedule adherence, documentation accuracy, follow-up completion, member engagement, and other departmental goals
  • Balance efficiency with careful listening, accurate problem-solving, and a respectful member experience
  • Remain available and focused during scheduled service periods and follow department practices regarding attendance, punctuality, breaks, workspace readiness, and phone coverage
  • Use approved standard operating procedures for activities such as training registration, benefit eligibility verification, member complaint intake, discipline-related inquiries, interpretation services, and case escalation
  • Participate in coaching, calibration, quality assurance, training, team meetings, and continuous-improvement activities
  • Identify recurring member questions, service gaps, process barriers, or system issues and share recommendations with MAC leadership
  • Collaborate with colleagues and other departments to support timely resolution, consistent communication, and strong member service
  • Maintain a clean, professional, secure, and distraction-free work environment
  • Perform other duties and special assignments as required to support the Member Action Center and the mission of SEIU Local 2015

title: Mobile Developer - Immich
description:
Job Description

Job Description

About Immich

Immich is on a mission to provide a secure, private home for your most precious memories through our high-performance, self-hosted photo and video backup solution. We're a lean, async team of 7 developers building software used by hundreds of thousands of people worldwide every day.

We move fast, care deeply about user experience, and build everything in the open. Our mobile apps are core to the Immich experience.

The Role

We are seeking a talented mobile developer with in-depth knowledge of native and cross platform mobile development. Our iOS and Android apps are built with Flutter. This is a high impact role where your work ships directly to hundreds of thousands of users. You'll tackle challenging problems in photo library integration, background synchronization, performance optimization, and native platform APIs.

The Team

You'll collaborate closely with the core team on architectural decisions and user interface design, and have real influence on the product roadmap.

What You'll Work On

- Building out the mobile app's capabilities to achieve feature parity with the web app
- Deep integration with native photo libraries: PHAsset (iOS) and MediaStore (Android)
- Background sync, upload pipelines, and memory-efficient media handling
- iCloud and Google Photos interop, including managing remote vs. local asset state
- Smooth, native-feeling UI: complex photo grids, timeline scrubbing, and gestures
- Performance profiling and optimization, i.e. startup time, scroll performance, and memory
- Crash reporting, ANR diagnosis, and production stability improvements

What We're Looking For

- Strong Flutter/Dart experience, with shipped production apps
- Solid understanding of mobile platform internals on iOS and/or Android
- Experience with native photo/media APIs (PHAsset, MediaStore, or equivalent)
- Comfort with async programming, isolates, and background processing patterns
- Experience with native background APIs (BGProcessingTask, WorkManager, etc.)
- Ability to work autonomously in a remote, async environment
- Clear, thoughtful communication, written and async-first

Nice to Have

- Experience with native Swift or Android development
- Familiarity with self-hosted software, homelab culture, or privacy-focused tools
- Open source contributions or public projects
- Experience with SQLite, database query optimization, or local-first architectures
- Background in photo or media applications

Why Immich
